text: tara: quick follow-up from research 1: micro-sparklines are hard to read in compact dashboards. legends wrap, tiny unit text truncates, and the little hint dots (outlier markers) have low contrast on some themes oliver: can you drop a screenshot? tara: attached to the ticket. two issues stood out: 1) the hint dots open individual tooltips if you mouse over, flooding the UI; 2) the tiny legend/units compress and show 't.../s' which confused a few participants nina: for the hint dots i'd prefer keeping visual markers but collapsing interactions into one summary affordance per-sparkline. keyboard & SR always target the summary, not each dot mark: agree. copy thought: call the compact label "peaks" or "spikes" in the micro UI. "anomalies" in docs. testers called them "spikes" more naturally ola: (typo) oliver: hehe. implementation idea: render markers in canvas/css, expose one ``` markers drawn on canvas, button is the only tabbable item tara: when the detail opens, trap focus in the panel and ensure the first focusable element is close to the timeline list. use aria-atomic so SR announces updated counts when data refreshes nina: microcopy: tiny inline legend uses abbreviations (Emb., Gen.) but tooltip / drawer shows full names. also change tiny CTA from "View details" -> "Open timeline" for compact contexts mark: dev/qa ask: can we get an a11y pass (VoiceOver + NVDA) on the prototype? especially check that only one keyboard stop exists and screen reader reads the P95 wording correctly design-bot: uploaded Figma variant + prototype: https://figma.redwood/compact-spark-hints/1795550000 ola: (again) oliver: i'll whip up the prototype with aria-hidden markers + one summary button and post a short demo GIF. will include high-contrast glyph variant tara: thanks. plan: oliver builds prototype -> nina + QA run SR passes -> finalize copy with PM -> ship behind prod-flag. estimate 1 dev day + 1 design day + half-day QA mark: leaving a note in the ticket to update telemetry names and include smoothing flag. also add a brief PR note about not using pointer-events hacks for accessibility tara: perfect, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
